quests.instruction: Cousins are staying for a week, and Mina's bed is given to one of them. What is a sensible way to adapt?
quests.correctAnswer: Sleep Where Arranged and Keep Her Things Tidy 🛏️
options: Insist on Having Her Own Bed Back Again Tonight 😠
Sleep Where Arranged and Keep Her Things Tidy 🛏️
Sleep in the Hallway Without Asking Anyone 🚪
quests.hint: Focus on being a good host in a shared space.
quests.explanation: Accepting the new arrangement and keeping her things tidy helps the visit go well. Insisting or sleeping in the hall without asking causes trouble.
quests.funFact: A roll-up mattress or a floor mat can turn a spare corner into a guest bed.

quests.instruction: Guests are coming for dinner at eight, and Dev still has maths homework. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Finish It Before the Guests Arrive 📚
options: Skip It Because Guests Are Coming 🙈
Do It at the Table During Dinner 🍽️
Finish It Before the Guests Arrive 📚
quests.hint: Ask yourself when he will be free to join the guests.
quests.explanation: Finishing before they arrive lets him enjoy the evening without a job hanging over him. Skipping it or doing it at the table is not fair to him or the guests.
quests.funFact: People in different countries have different ideas about how punctual guests should be.

quests.instruction: A guest arrives early while Ravi is still finishing his chores. What is a good way to handle it?
quests.correctAnswer: Greet Them, Then Finish the Chores Quickly 👋
options: Greet Them, Then Finish the Chores Quickly 👋
Ignore the Guest and Carry On with the Chores 🧹
Hide in His Room Until the Guest Leaves 🙈
quests.hint: Focus on welcoming first and finishing second.
quests.explanation: Greeting the guest shows respect, and he can finish the chores quickly afterwards. Hiding or ignoring them would seem unwelcoming.
quests.funFact: In Thailand, people greet each other with a 'wai', pressing their palms together and bowing slightly.

quests.instruction: The family is about to leave for the railway station. Which check is the most important?
quests.correctAnswer: Tickets and ID Are Together in One Place 🎫
options: The Favourite Toy Is Packed in the Bag Safely 🧸
Tickets and ID Are Together in One Place 🎫
All the Windows Are Left Open Wide at Home 🪟
quests.hint: Work out what you cannot travel without.
quests.explanation: Without tickets and ID the family may not be allowed to travel, so they are kept together and checked. A toy is nice but not essential, and open windows are a risk.
quests.funFact: Ticket checkers on trains may ask to see ID along with the ticket.

quests.instruction: At the station, the platform for the train is changed at the last minute. What should the family do?
quests.correctAnswer: Stay Together and Follow Signs or Staff 🚉
options: Stay Together and Follow Signs or Staff 🚉
Stop and Wait Where They Are Standing 🕰️
Run Ahead Alone to Find the Platform 🏃
quests.hint: Think about getting there safely as a group.
quests.explanation: Staying together and following signs or station staff gets everyone to the right platform. Running ahead alone or waiting would risk someone being lost or missing the train.
quests.funFact: Large stations use announcements and screens so that passengers can find changed platforms.

quests.instruction: On a night train, Tia has to sleep somewhere unfamiliar. What helps her settle?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep a Familiar Toy or Book Nearby 🧸
options: Stay Up Watching Videos on a Phone 📱
Refuse to Sleep Until They Get Home 😠
Keep a Familiar Toy or Book Nearby 🧸
quests.hint: Ask yourself what makes a new place feel familiar.
quests.explanation: Familiar things bring comfort in a new place and help her relax. Refusing to sleep or watching videos keeps her awake.
quests.funFact: Psychologists sometimes call a child's comfort toy a 'transitional object'.

quests.instruction: School starts again tomorrow after a long holiday, and Anu has been going to bed very late. What would have been the best preparation?
quests.correctAnswer: Shift Bedtime Earlier a Little Each Night 🌙
options: Change Everything on the Last Night Only 😴
Shift Bedtime Earlier a Little Each Night 🌙
Stay Up Late and Hope to Cope Fine 🥱
quests.hint: Ask yourself how the body adjusts to a new sleep time.
quests.explanation: Moving bedtime a little at a time lets the body clock adjust gently. Changing everything on the last night or hoping to cope makes the first day harder.
quests.funFact: The body clock adjusts slowly, which is why a sudden change in sleep time can leave people feeling groggy.

quests.instruction: After the holiday, Hari has forgotten some of what he learned. What helps him settle back in?
quests.correctAnswer: Look Over His Notes and Ask the Teacher 📓
options: Pretend He Remembers Everything Perfectly 🙈
Look Over His Notes and Ask the Teacher 📓
Skip Lessons Until He Feels Ready Again 🏠
quests.hint: Remember how to refresh memory and get help.
quests.explanation: Reviewing notes and asking questions refreshes his memory quickly. Pretending or skipping lessons makes the gaps bigger.
quests.funFact: Teachers often begin a new term with a quick review, because everyone forgets some things over a break.

quests.instruction: Before the first day back, Meera finds her lunch box was left with food in it last term. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Wash and Check It Before Day One 🍱
options: Buy a New One Every Single Day 🛍️
Use It Dirty and Hope for the Best 🙈
Wash and Check It Before Day One 🍱
quests.hint: Think about food left in a box for weeks.
quests.explanation: A box left with food can be unsafe and smelly, so it must be washed and checked before use. Using it dirty is not safe.
quests.funFact: Food left in a closed container for weeks can grow mould, which is why old lunch boxes should be cleaned out.

quests.instruction: School has moved lunch break from one o'clock to half past twelve. How can children adapt?
quests.correctAnswer: Have an Earlier Breakfast or a Small Snack 🍎
options: Ignore the Change and Just Feel Hungry Later 🙈
Skip Lunch Altogether to Save Some Time 🚫
Have an Earlier Breakfast or a Small Snack 🍎
quests.hint: Consider how the change affects hunger.
quests.explanation: A small snack or earlier breakfast helps them feel ready for the earlier lunch. Ignoring the change or skipping lunch leaves them hungry.
quests.funFact: Schools set break times to fit the timetable, which is why they sometimes change.

quests.instruction: Hari now gets home before his mother. What helps him most?
quests.correctAnswer: Agree a Plan with His Family 📝
options: Wait Outside the Gate Until It Is Dark 🌙
Agree a Plan with His Family 📝
Invite Friends Over Without Asking First 🙄
quests.hint: Remember who needs to know what he will do.
quests.explanation: A plan agreed with family covers what to do on arriving, who to call and what to do first. Inviting friends without asking or waiting outside is not safe.
quests.funFact: Writing things down can help memory, because the act of writing makes people think about the words.

quests.instruction: The school has a new rule that phones must stay in lockers during the day. How should Mina respond?
quests.correctAnswer: Follow the Rule and Keep It in the Locker 🔒
options: Argue with the Teachers Until the Rule Changes 😠
Hide It in Her Pocket and Use It Quietly 🤫
Follow the Rule and Keep It in the Locker 🔒
quests.hint: Decide how rules work in a school.
quests.explanation: Following the rule keeps things fair for everyone. Hiding the phone or arguing does not change the rule and can lead to trouble.
quests.funFact: Some schools have locker rules for phones so that students can focus in lessons.

quests.instruction: The water supply is off for two hours. How should the family adapt?
quests.correctAnswer: Use Stored Water for Drinking and Washing Hands 🪣
options: Use Water Freely for Everything Until It Runs Out 🚿
Use Stored Water for Drinking and Washing Hands 🪣
Go Without Drinking at All Until It Returns 🚫
quests.hint: The clue is which uses are the most essential.
quests.explanation: Stored water should go to the most important uses first, like drinking and hand washing. Using it freely wastes it, and going without drinking is unsafe.
quests.funFact: An adult needs roughly two litres of fluid a day, so a store of water should be planned on that basis.

quests.instruction: The internet is down at homework time. What is a sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Do Reading and Written Tasks First 📖
options: Do Reading and Written Tasks First 📖
Use a Neighbour's Wi-Fi Without Asking 📶
Give Up for the Whole Evening 🏳️
quests.hint: Decide which tasks need no connection.
quests.explanation: Reading and written work do not need the internet, so she can still make progress. Giving up or using someone's Wi-Fi without asking is not helpful or fair.
quests.funFact: The internet works through cables, including undersea ones, that carry data between countries.

quests.instruction: The washing machine has broken, and Dev's second uniform is not clean. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask the Teacher About Clean Clothes 👕
options: Ask the Teacher About Clean Clothes 👕
Wear the Dirty One Without Saying 🙈
Skip School Until It Is Fixed 🏠
quests.hint: The clue is who can say what is acceptable.
quests.explanation: Telling the teacher explains the problem and lets the school say what is allowed. Wearing a dirty uniform or missing school does not help.
quests.funFact: Schools usually accept a short note or message from a parent that explains a problem like a broken washing machine.

quests.instruction: Aman has thirty minutes before dinner and three jobs: homework due tomorrow, tidying his room and practising guitar. Which should he do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Homework, Because It Is Due Tomorrow 📚
options: Tidying, Because It Is Quick to Do 🧹
Homework, Because It Is Due Tomorrow 📚
Guitar, Because It Is Fun to Play 🎸
quests.hint: Consider which job has a deadline.
quests.explanation: Homework is due tomorrow, so it comes first. Guitar and tidying can follow or happen another day.
quests.funFact: A well-known planning tool, the Eisenhower matrix, sorts tasks into urgent and important.

quests.instruction: A friend visits unexpectedly while Mina still has a chore to finish. What is a considerate approach?
quests.correctAnswer: Finish It Quickly and Invite Her to Wait 🧹
options: Finish It Quickly and Invite Her to Wait 🧹
Ask the Friend to Do the Chore for Her 🙄
Leave It Undone and Forget About It 🙈
quests.hint: Think about the chore and the friend together.
quests.explanation: Finishing quickly keeps her promise, and the friend is welcomed. Forgetting it or asking the friend to do it is not fair.
quests.funFact: A kitchen timer set for ten minutes is a popular way to keep a short chore from dragging on.

quests.instruction: Two classmates need help with their work, but Leo only has time for one before the bell. What is a fair way to handle it?
quests.correctAnswer: Help One Now and Offer the Other Later 🤝
options: Help One Now and Offer the Other Later 🤝
Try to Help Both and Be Late to Class 🕰️
Help Neither and Rush Off to Class 🏃
quests.hint: Focus on being honest about what he can do.
quests.explanation: Helping one properly and offering the other time later is fair and realistic. Helping neither or trying both could mean no one gets proper help.
quests.funFact: 'Under-promise and over-deliver' is a business saying about doing a little more than you said you would.

quests.instruction: Dev is at home with his grandfather, who suddenly feels dizzy and has to sit down. What should Dev do?
quests.correctAnswer: Get Another Grown-up or Call for Help 📞
options: Give Him Medicine from the Cupboard 💊
Wait Quietly Until a Parent Gets Home 🤞
Get Another Grown-up or Call for Help 📞
quests.hint: Think about who is able to decide what to do.
quests.explanation: A dizzy person may need medical help, and a child should get a grown-up or call for help straight away. Giving medicine or waiting is risky.
quests.funFact: Staying calm and speaking clearly helps emergency operators understand what is happening.

quests.instruction: A smoke alarm sounds loudly in the middle of the night, and there is a smell of smoke. What should the family do?
quests.correctAnswer: Leave Quickly and Meet at a Planned Spot 🚪
options: Search the House for Pets and Favourite Toys 🧸
Hide Under the Bed and Wait for Help 🛏️
Leave Quickly and Meet at a Planned Spot 🚪
quests.hint: Focus on getting everyone out safely.
quests.explanation: Getting out quickly and meeting at a planned spot keeps everyone safe and lets grown-ups count heads. Going back inside or hiding wastes precious time.
quests.funFact: Home fire plans usually include two ways out of every room and a place to meet outside.

quests.instruction: Meera gets a nosebleed in class. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell the Teacher and Lean Slightly Forward 🩸
options: Tell the Teacher and Lean Slightly Forward 🩸
Tip Her Head Far Back and Look at the Ceiling 🙄
Stuff Lots of Tissue Deep Inside Her Nose 🧻
quests.hint: Consider keeping blood from running down the throat.
quests.explanation: Leaning forward keeps blood from running down the throat, and the teacher can help. Tilting back or pushing tissue deep inside is not recommended.
quests.funFact: Nosebleeds are common in children and usually stop on their own within about ten minutes.

quests.instruction: It is exam week. How can Anu adapt her evening routine?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep Meals and Sleep, and Add Short Study Blocks 📚
options: Stop Studying Completely Because Exams Are Stressful 🏳️
Skip Sleep to Fit In Much More Study Time 🌙
Keep Meals and Sleep, and Add Short Study Blocks 📚
quests.hint: Consider what helps the brain work well on exam day.
quests.explanation: Meals and sleep help the brain work well, and short study blocks add practice. Skipping sleep or giving up both hurt her chances.
quests.funFact: Studying in short blocks with breaks helps people remember more than one long unbroken session.

quests.instruction: On the morning of an exam, which plan is best for Rohan?
quests.correctAnswer: Eat Breakfast and Arrive Early, Kit Ready ✏️
options: Arrive Just at the Very Last Minute Possible 🏃
Eat Breakfast and Arrive Early, Kit Ready ✏️
Skip Breakfast to Revise a Bit More Instead 📖
quests.hint: Think about starting the exam calm and ready.
quests.explanation: Breakfast gives energy, and arriving early with materials ready means a calm start. Skipping food or arriving late adds stress.
quests.funFact: Exam rooms often have a clock so that students can keep track of time.

quests.instruction: After an exam, Rohan realises he made a mistake on one question. What is a helpful response?
quests.correctAnswer: Learn From It and Move On to the Next Paper 📝
options: Learn From It and Move On to the Next Paper 📝
Blame the Teacher for Setting Such a Question 👈
Stay Upset About It for the Rest of the Day 😞
quests.hint: Think about what he can still influence.
quests.explanation: Learning from the mistake helps next time, and moving on keeps him focused on the next paper. Blaming or dwelling on it does not.
quests.funFact: Going over mistakes after an exam is one way to find out which topics need more practice.

quests.instruction: On festival day, the family eats later than usual and the house is busy. Which part of the routine matters most to keep?
quests.correctAnswer: Drinking Enough Water and Getting Some Rest 💧
options: Drinking Enough Water and Getting Some Rest 💧
Doing the Daily Chores in the Same Order 🧹
Eating at the Usual Time Whatever Happens 🕐
quests.hint: Think about what the body needs on a long, busy day.
quests.explanation: Water and rest look after the body on a long, busy day, even when mealtimes move. Eating at a fixed time or keeping the chore order is less important.
quests.funFact: On hot, busy days the body can lose water without us noticing, so drinking regularly matters.

quests.instruction: Fireworks are being lit outside. How should the children stay safe?
quests.correctAnswer: Watch from a Safe Distance 🎆
options: Stand Close to Get a Better View 👀
Pick Up Ones That Did Not Go Off 🧨
Watch from a Safe Distance 🎆
quests.hint: Think about how far away you need to be.
quests.explanation: Fireworks can burst unpredictably, so a safe distance and grown-ups handling them is best. Standing close or picking up duds is dangerous.
quests.funFact: A firework that has not gone off can still explode, so it should be left alone.

quests.instruction: After a late festival night, school is tomorrow. What is a sensible plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Plan a Calm Evening and an Early Bedtime 🛏️
options: Plan a Calm Evening and an Early Bedtime 🛏️
Skip School Without Telling Anyone 🏠
Stay Up Even Later to Keep Celebrating 🌙
quests.hint: Consider catching up on rest.
quests.explanation: A calm evening and an early bedtime help the body catch up on rest before school. Staying up later or skipping school does not.
quests.funFact: Missing sleep for one night can be made up with a calm day and a good night's rest.

quests.instruction: Plans have changed three times today. What helps Ravi keep track?
quests.correctAnswer: Write the New Plan Down and Check It 📝
options: Just Remember Everything in His Head Alone 🧠
Ask Other People to Decide for Him 🙄
Write the New Plan Down and Check It 📝
quests.hint: Decide how to avoid forgetting changes.
quests.explanation: Writing the plan down keeps the latest version clear. Relying on memory or on others can lead to mix-ups.
quests.funFact: Lists and notes help people remember changes because they take the load off memory.

quests.instruction: Which statement is true about adapting routines?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep the Purpose, Change the Details 🎯
options: Change Absolutely Everything Every Time 🔄
Keep the Purpose, Change the Details 🎯
Never Change Anything Under Any Plan 🔒
quests.hint: Work out what stays the same when a plan changes.
quests.explanation: A routine's purpose, such as being ready, safe or rested, stays the same while details like time or place change.
quests.funFact: A football team may change its formation at half-time, but its goal stays the same.

quests.instruction: Which is the best sign that a routine has been adapted well?
quests.correctAnswer: Important Things Still Get Done in a New Way ✅
options: Everything Was Skipped and Then Forgotten About 🙈
Important Things Still Get Done in a New Way ✅
Nothing Changed at All, Anywhere, for Anyone 🔒
quests.hint: The key is the result, not the method.
quests.explanation: A good adaptation still gets the important things done, even if the method changed. No change or skipping everything are not adaptations.
quests.funFact: A goal that is written down is easier to remember and track.
